angle_en: Deep seeing ends in surrender to the one reality in all things.

en.intro: Krishna now says that the wise one who sees the divine everywhere and surrenders is very rare. Listen for that word.
en.notice: Vasudeva is the name of the divine, and it means the one who dwells everywhere. The wise one who sees that Vasudeva is everything and surrenders is what Krishna calls rare.
en.next: Krishna then explains that those whose understanding is clouded by desire turn to other radiant beings instead.
en.meaning: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.

hi.intro: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि सब कुछ परमात्मा को देखने वाला और समर्पण करने वाला ज्ञानी बहुत दुर्लभ है। इस दुर्लभ शब्द को सुनिए।
hi.meaning: बहुत जन्मोंके अन्तमें अर्थात् मनुष्यजन्ममें सब कुछ परमात्मा ही है, ऐसा जो ज्ञानवान् मेरे शरण होता है, वह महात्मा अत्यन्त दुर्लभ है ॥
hi.notice: वासुदेव नाम का अर्थ है जो सब जगह रहता है। जो ज्ञानी यह जानता है कि वासुदेव ही सब कुछ है और मेरे शरण आता है, उसे कृष्ण दुर्लभ कहते हैं।
hi.next: संजय कहते हैं कि जो लोग अपनी समझ खोकर इच्छाओं के पीछे चलते हैं, वे दूसरे देवताओं की शरण लेते हैं।
hi.angle_hi: वासुदेव ही सब कुछ है, दुर्लभ आत्मा

en.intro: Krishna now says that the wise one who sees the divine everywhere and surrenders is very rare. Listen for that word.
en.body: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare. Vasudeva is the name of the divine, and it means the one who dwells everywhere. The wise one who sees that Vasudeva is everything and surrenders is what Krishna calls rare. Krishna then explains that those whose understanding is clouded by desire turn to other radiant beings instead.

issues: borrowed: "कृष्ण आगे कहते हैं कि जो लोग अपनी समझ खोकर इच्छाओं के पीछे चलते हैं, वे दूसरे देवताओं की शरण लेते हैं।" (This is the content of the NEXT verse (verse 20), not verse 19. It has been incorrectly placed in the notice section of verse 19.)

borrowed: "संजय कहते हैं कि जो लोग अपनी समझ खोकर इच्छाओं के पीछे चलते हैं, वे दूसरे देवताओं की शरण लेते हैं।" (The notice in the Hindi script attributes the explanation of desire-driven people turning to other deities to Sanjay (the narrator), whereas the source verse (7.20) is spoken by Krishna, not Sanjay.)

meaning_changed: "कृष्ण कहते हैं कि सब कुछ परमात्मा को देखने वाला और समर्पण करने वाला ज्ञानी बहुत दुर्लभ है।" (The Hindi intro omits the crucial context of 'after many births' (बहुोंं जन्मनाम् अन्ते) and the specific realization that Vasudeva is everything. It frames the rarity as a general statement about any wise person who sees the divine and surrenders, rather than the specific rare soul who has matured through many births to see Vasudeva in all things.)
